method: Both reviewers read every German string of the unit again, including the ones r2 asked to change. That covered title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, recapDe, the Folge (9 lines) and its gist item, the LS1 and LS2 dialogues (10 lines each), the LS3 chat, the 6 H1 texts, the strategy card, the 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (situation, instructions, cards), aiRole, openingLine, the 8 hintWords and the 15 modelTurns, the S1 task (title, situation, taskDe, 5 labels, checklist, model), the 2 check lines, story.beat and the cliffhanger, every endLine and modelSentence and every explanation. We also read the 35 u01 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json and the rule cards rc.praesens and rc.verbposition-2. We solved all 99 authored items blind from promptDe plus their options, tiles or audio line (start gist 1, input 15, structured 12, pool 37, reserve 15, exam 6, check 9, proof 4) and the 5 S1 fields. For every sentence_building item we permuted the tiles and checked each V2 order against accepted[]. We graded candidate answers with src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js itself (quoted in F06 and previousFindings). We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>; 12 units compiled, nothing written to the repo). We then ran the server's own normalizeSpeakingTask, buildCoursePartnerPrompt and grade.mjs criteriaPlan on the compiled a11-u01-s entry and listed every A1.1 bank entry that carries `parts` (F01). LEX-01 does not walk recapDe, the Folge, story.beat, openingLine, hintWords, modelTurns, redemittel, the S1 title/labels/model, modelSentences, readAloud lines or lexicon card examples. We measured those surfaces with the validator's own knownForms, licensedForms, knownCompound and INSTRUCTION_METALANGUAGE (lib-validate/lexicon.mjs, rules/LEX-01.mjs unknownOnSurface). All unit surfaces are now known words. The only unknown tokens are on lexicon cards (F05) and in rule-card prose (which has its English twin). We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1, sp1, sp2, s1) and the rubric files sd1-sp1, sd1-sp2, sd1-s1, course-micro and course-micro-sp. We also counted the distinct speakers of every H1 text in u01, u02 and u04 (F07). We read the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json and curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U1, and the new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new entries, productive share 0.5, sentences ≤ 12 words). We read the can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json, the cast against casts/a1.json and series.json, and the story hand-over against the u02 Folge and story. Every fix proposed below was measured before it was recommended: validator wordCount for the rewritten H1 texts (t4 40, t5 35, t6 46 words, all in [32–53]), known-token status of every inserted word, the LS2 word total (133, unchanged) and the ≤ 25-word explanation cap. We re-read the u04 exemplar trail (r1–r5) and checked each of its finding classes here (notes). No 360 px walkthrough was run; that is the walkthrough reviewer's remit.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 2 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 6 MINOR. On the unit side this was a good fix round. Of the unit edits r2 asked for, all but three landed: the second „sich vorstellen“ input, „Pristina“ and Priya's Malayalam in the Sp1 model. The German on every unit surface is correct. Every one of the 99 keys is right, and every German-only surface now uses known words, including the cliffhanger. S1, Sp1 and Sp2 match sd1.json, and every task is original. What stops exit is almost entirely outside the unit file. The same four owner-held points have been open since r1 or r2, and nobody who can fix them has acted. (1) F01, blocker and stop-the-line. The speaking engine still ignores `parts` and grades the whole session with sd1-sp1, which still scores „buchstabieren“ and „nummer“. The Sp2 round, which is the unit's Aufgabe proof of asking and saying goodbye, is therefore neither run as designed nor scored, and a flawless session still shows at most „1 von 3“. The same holds in all 8 A1.1 units with a multi-Teil task, so A1.1 cannot be declared finished until the E1 server track and the rubric owner land this. (2) F02, blocker. specs.json still describes the pre-r1 unit (Sp1 full, no Sp2, SMS), so the validator exits 1 on COV-3. (3) F03 and F04, both MAJOR. The u01 word card still makes Emre speak English, and the LS2 rule card still models „Was sprechen Sie?“, for the third round running. The six minors are: the lexicon roles and examples (owner), the Pristina spelling and one explanation fragment, H1 texts t4–t6 with three voices where Hören Teil 1 has two (new), five small scene breaks, detector noise (rule-smith and spine) and the missing verb-ending ErrorTag (SCHEMA). Another content round on u01 cannot close F01–F04, because the unit author may not write those files. They must reach their owners before round 4, or round 4 will fail on the same points.

findings.problem: Nothing has changed since r2, and the rubric half has been open since r1. The unit has done its part. It marks Sp1 'reduced', puts the Teil 2 script and both card sets into aiRole.personaDe, and ends Sp2 with „Danke! Auf Wiedersehen!“. The server still reads only the top-level template, mode and profile that the compiler copies from parts[0], so the model now gets contradictory instructions. The persona prose describes two card rounds, but the ABLAUF block, the prompt's procedural rule, says: let the learner speak alone, then ask one or two follow-up questions. There is no SITUATION or AUFGABE line, and the learner's cards reach the model only as persona prose. Whether Teil 2 happens at all depends on which instruction the model follows. Grading is unchanged. The whole transcript is scored with sd1-sp1 alone. The Teil 2 questions and answers (sd1-sp2: 2 points per question and 1 per answer, 6 in all) have no criterion. buchstabieren and nummer are scored although the unit tells the learner they come in Einheit 2. A flawless session therefore shows at most „1 von 3 Punkten (Richtwert)“. That is a scorer on the wrong pass rule for both Teile (§9.4 BLOCKER). It also means cd.a1.person-erfragen and cd.a1.verabschieden, whose Aufgabe proof is this round, are never scored. The class covers 8 of the 12 A1.1 units, including the u04 exemplar (graded with sd1-sp2 only, Sp3 unscored). It is stop-the-line (§9.4), and A1.1 cannot be reported as finished while it stands.

E1 server track: normalizeSpeakingTask keeps `parts` and normalises each part. buildCoursePartnerPrompt renders one ABLAUF per part, in order, each with that part's situation, instructions and both card sets, plus a hand-over line („Danke! Jetzt Teil 2.“). cards-ask runs round by round: the learner asks with the round's card, the partner answers, then the partner asks with its card and the learner answers. speakingV2 grades each part with its own profile and sums the scores, and ResultCard shows the score per Teil. Rubric owner: a SpeakingPart declares the criteria it elicits, or buchstabieren and nummer get appliesIf 'full' and appliesTo honours a 'reduced' Prüfungsfokus length. u01 is then scored out of 1 + 6. Unit: no edit. After the fix, play one u01 session and check three things: the AI runs Teil 2 with the learner's cards, it ends with „Danke! Auf Wiedersehen!“, and the result card shows both Teile.
